title: [1980s style inverse platformer] The Curse of the Tomb
author: Robonotes1760

comments.author: Robonotes1760
comments.body: For a little more insight into the workflow: this was all done in MS Teams Copilot with GPT 5.5 "think deep". It took about a week of evenings plus most of the week-end. The AI's initial architecture was not good: the AI player's pathfinding was the most difficult part. The LLM initially produced a lot of conflicts between planning and execution. I had to tell it in terms to produce a graph of all reachable routes, to include the enemies in those routes, to allow for a range of specific classes of mistake at <100% skill (including delayed reactions to new enemy deployments, mistimed jumps, and, at very low skill levels, going lemming off the edge on maps with an edge void). I had to tell it in terms to plan once and only once when enemies were deployed (as they all have a simple deterministic path, as in real 1980s platform games)  and execute that plan exactly without deviation. This took >300 iterations to get right, initially with placeholder graphics, adding the final graphics later.
